stories.title: NYC mayor unveils plan to close notorious Rikers Island jail by 2032
stories.summary: Rikers had been slated to close by August 2027 following legislation passed by the City Council in 2019. Moving the deadline will require a change to this law.

stories.title: Turkey: Activists chant 'shame' as COP31 negotiations falter
stories.summary: Climate activists denounced the proposed outcome of COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, on Friday 20 November 2026, accusing governments of failing to deliver meaningful progress on tackling climate change. They chanted "shame" as negotiations approached their deadline.

stories.title: Miami or Vice City? Tour the real-world inspiration for GTA 6
stories.summary: BBC News Mundo’s Rafael Rojas visits the real-life Miami locations that inspired Vice City, GTA 6’s fictionalised setting.

stories.title: What the new UK-EU deal could mean for future post-Brexit relations
stories.summary: The BBC's political and Europe editors analyse the new agreements between the UK and EU.

stories.title: Tech stock sell-off drags markets down as Anthropic shares slide
stories.summary: Pressures weighed on US markets, with the S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average pushed into correction territory.

stories.title: In a year of AI solving maths problems, an Anthropic worker says he may have cracked the biggest
stories.summary: A mathematician at Anthropic says he used an AI to prove the famed Riemann hypothesis, though verification will take some time.

stories.title: These dead pets were meant to be cremated - then their bodies appeared on a livestream
stories.summary: Grieving Filipinos confront a distressing reality: their dogs and cats may not have received the send-off they paid for.

stories.title: Mamdani announces plan to close New York's Rikers Island jail by 2032
stories.summary: Plans to shutter the troubled facility date back to 2019, when the city council first voted to close it but delays arose over where to place inmates.

stories.title: ANC fights to keep control of South Africa's key cities after election setback
stories.summary: The ANC appears reluctant to replicate its national power-sharing deal with the pro-business DA at the local level.

stories.title: Hashim Thaci's second conviction in The Hague reignites debate in Kosovo about justice and the Kosovo Specialist Chambers
stories.summary: Former President Hashim Thaci has been convicted of trying to influence witnesses in his war crimes trial. The conviction has reignited debate in Kosovo about the Kosovo Specialist Chambers, the court that convicted him.

stories.title: Uganda minister at COP31: 'We need a just transition'
stories.summary: Funding from wealthy countries to help deal with the impacts of climate change hasn't materialized, says Uganda's environment minister. The East African country is hoping oil and carbon credits will help boost finances.

stories.summary: Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report. stories.summary: Al-Qadisiyah University’s move a sign of the country’s slide into a Taliban-like gender segregation, say activists The removal of male professors teaching female students at a university in southern Iraq has sparked protests and been criticised by activists as a Taliban-like gender segregation policy. stories.title: Rights court rules Turkey must release jailed lawmaker Atalay
stories.summary: The European Court of Human Rights has called for the release of imprisoned elected lawmaker Can Atalay. Atalay has been in prison for almost five years despite rulings from the Turkish Constitutional Court.

stories.title: How a green economy could help reverse climate change
stories.summary: Green growth promises a future in which economies thrive without destroying the environment. But is this vision realistic?

stories.title: Borussia Dortmund bows to fan pressure and end Rheinmetall deal
stories.summary: Borussia Dortmund has reluctantly ended its association with a major sponsor after long-term fan protests. They are not the first Bundesliga club to u-turn, as commercial interests clash with politics and fan culture.

stories.title: Is the AI bubble bursting just as Anthropic goes public?
stories.summary: The sharp sell-off in tech stocks after the US midterms and the Nvidia scandal has cast doubt on Anthropic's IPO. Yet with hundreds of billions still being invested, some think the AI party is still in full swing.

stories.title: Anthropic trading tests investors' appetite for AI
stories.summary: Anthropic was valued at $2 trillion after shares started trading on the Nasdaq following a record $81 billion IPO. Its performance will put investor confidence in AI to the test.

stories.title: No mention of fossil fuels in latest COP31 draft deal
stories.summary: One of the most fraught debates at the UN climate talks in Turkey has revolved around the future of coal, oil and gas. Now, all mention of fossil fuels has been removed from the summit's new draft agreement.

stories.title: Police clash with protesters during Spain's general strike – video
stories.summary: Clashes between protesters and police erupted in the streets of Barcelona and Madrid on 11 November as millions of Spanish workers took part in Spain's first general strike in 14 years to protest the country's housing affordability crisis less than three weeks before a snap general election.
